description: Proofs about degrees, trees and minimum spanning trees

puzzles.title: \text{Prove the handshake lemma: } \sum_{v \in V} \deg(v) = 2|E|
puzzles.statement: \text{In every finite simple graph } G = (V, E) \text{, } \sum_{v \in V} \deg(v) = 2|E|.

blocks.latex: \text{We count the pairs } (v, e) \text{ where vertex } v \text{ is an endpoint of edge } e \text{, in two ways.}
\text{First, by vertex: vertex } v \text{ is an endpoint of exactly } \deg(v) \text{ edges.}
\text{So the number of pairs is } \sum_{v \in V} \deg(v).
\text{Next, by edge: every edge } e = \{u, w\} \text{ has exactly two endpoints, since } u \ne w.
\text{So the number of pairs is also } 2|E|.
\text{Both counts are of the same pairs, so } \sum_{v \in V} \deg(v) {{op:=}} 2|E|.

puzzles.title: \text{Prove: a tree with } n \text{ vertices has } n - 1 \text{ edges}
puzzles.displayTitle: Prove: a tree on n vertices has n − 1 edges
puzzles.statement: \text{Every tree (connected graph with no cycles) with } n \ge 1 \text{ vertices has exactly } n - 1 \text{ edges.}

blocks.latex: \text{Proof by induction on } n \ge 1.
\textbf{Base case: } n = 1 \text{: a single vertex has no edges, and } 1 - 1 = 0.
\textbf{Inductive step: } \text{assume every tree with } k \text{ vertices has } k - 1 \text{ edges, for some } k \ge 1.
\text{Let } T \text{ be a tree with } k + 1 \ge 2 \text{ vertices.}
\text{Take a longest path in } T \text{. Its last vertex } v \text{ has degree 1, since any other neighbour would extend the path or close a cycle. So } v \text{ is a leaf.}
\text{Remove } v \text{ and its single edge to get } T'.
T' \text{ is still connected, because no path between two other vertices passes through the leaf } v \text{, and it has no cycles. So } T' \text{ is a tree with } k \text{ vertices.}
\text{By the inductive hypothesis, } T' \text{ has } k - 1 \text{ edges.}
\text{Adding back the edge at } v \text{, } T \text{ has } (k - 1) + 1 = k {{op:=}} (k + 1) - 1 \text{ edges.}
\text{Therefore, by induction, a tree with } n \text{ vertices has } n - 1 \text{ edges } {{quantifier:\forall}} n {{op:\geq}} 1.

puzzles.title: \text{Prove the cut property of minimum spanning trees}
puzzles.statement: \text{Let } G = (V, E) \text{ be a connected weighted graph and } (S, V \setminus S) \text{ a cut. If } e \text{ has minimum weight among the edges crossing the cut, some minimum spanning tree contains } e.

blocks.latex: \text{Let } e = \{u, v\} \text{ with } u \in S \text{ and } v \in V \setminus S \text{, and let } T \text{ be any minimum spanning tree.}
\text{If } e \in T \text{, we are done. Otherwise } e {{setop:\notin}} T.
\text{Adding } e \text{ to } T \text{ creates exactly one cycle: } e \text{ together with the path from } u \text{ to } v \text{ in } T.
\text{That path starts in } S \text{ and ends in } V \setminus S \text{, so it contains an edge } e' \text{ that also crosses the cut.}
\text{Let } T' = T - e' + e \text{. Removing an edge of the cycle keeps the graph connected, and } T' \text{ has } {|V| - 1} \text{ edges, so } T' \text{ is a spanning tree.}
\text{Since } e \text{ has minimum weight among crossing edges, } w(e) \le w(e') \text{, so } w(T') = w(T) - w(e') + w(e) {{op:\leq}} w(T).
\text{Since } T \text{ is a minimum spanning tree, also } w(T) \le w(T') \text{, so } w(T') = w(T).
\text{So } T' \text{ is a minimum spanning tree, and it contains } e.
